High-throughput genotyping of samples from 16 of 26 provinces (100–200 patients per sentinel clinic) using MOSAIC reveals few Pfk13 variants linked to artemisinin resistance, but marked geographic variation in partner-drug resistance markers Pfcrt and Pfmdr1. In eastern provinces bordering the Great Lakes, Pfcrt/Pfmdr1 markers associated with 4-aminoquinoline resistance are common, indicating higher risk of artesunate-amodiaquine failure. In northern and southern regions, Pfmdr1 and Pfcrt haplotypes linked to artemether-lumefantrine failure predominate. The study supports integrating genomic surveillance with sentinel networks to tailor malaria treatment and chemoprevention at administrative level 1, offering early warnings of emerging resistance as of 2026-11-20.

articleHeadline: Small Molecules Target Nucleocapsid Protein to Block Crimean-Congo
articleSummary: Small-molecule inhibitors target the Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) nucleocapsid (N) protein, disrupting RNA encapsidation and N-mediated viral mRNA translation in cell culture. A high-throughput screen of 108,947 compounds yielded 122 inhibitors, 86 dose-responsive, and 37 confirmed hits; three were prioritized (11, 14, 33). In vitro, they noncompetitively inhibit N binding to the 5' UTR hairpin with IC50 11–41 μM and show CC50 >1–2 mM. In the Hazara virus surrogate (BSL-2), EC50s are 23–51 μM with selectivity indices 34–86. Plaque assays revealed >100-fold reductions for 11 and 14; 33 nearly abolishes detectable virus. Mechanistic assays indicate activity in post-entry replication by blocking N-mediated translation enhancement without disrupting host translation. Modeling points to compound 11 binding the N stalk–head interface (Gln300, Glu240, Lys473). These compounds offer leads for optimization; there are no approved antivirals or vaccines for CCHFV.

articleHeadline: PBO Restores Insecticide Sensitivity in Resistant Ghanaian Malaria Vectors
articleSummary: In Ghana's forest-savannah transition zone, Anopheles gambiae s.s. dominate in Kintampo North Municipality and Kintampo South District. Multiclass insecticide resistance is observed: malathion (5%) induces 100% mortality at 24 hours, while propoxur (1%), DDT (4%), and alpha-cypermethrin (0.05%) yield mortality below WHO susceptibility thresholds. Intensity bioassays show high-intensity pyrethroid resistance, with mortality remaining under 98% even at tenfold diagnostic alpha-cypermethrin concentration. Implications point to potential use of PBO-treated nets and organophosphate tools, pending field validation. The study fills surveillance gaps in Ghana's malaria transmission belt and underscores the need for continued entomological, epidemiological, and programmatic evaluations before deployment.

articleHeadline: Bacterial Pathogens Detected Across Urban and Peri-Urban Mammals in Greater
articleSummary: Across urban Legon and Madina and the peri-urban Dodowa in Ghana’s Greater Accra Region, a molecular screening of 404 mammals (185 dogs, 15 cats, 204 free-living rodents) conducted December 2019–October 2020 found widespread carriage of zoonotic bacteria.
